messages:
Alex Chen: IncidentBot just paged me for sustained inference-queue latency in eu-west-1. Root cause looks like a rapid drop in available GPU capacity for pool-gpu-eu-a; eviction spikes and autoscaler thrash. Customers seeing elevated 95th percentile latencies and some 429s reported on shared-hosted routes. pinging oncall: @Sam (oncall).

IncidentBot: PAGE: elevated_inference_latency_eu-west-1 — severity: high — triggered at 1920004321 — affected services: inference-api-hosted, model-routing. Link: https://incident.internal/1920004321

Sam (oncall): I'm on it. Checking cluster health and autoscaler logs. First glance: a single host went into maintenance mode then cloud preemptions overlapped with a node pool scale-in. Starting timeline reconstruction.

Mira Patel: Can you confirm customer impact? Any high-value tenants routed to this pool? Priya, FYI for support comms.

Priya (support lead): Support: we have 3 escalations in EU reporting timeouts. Escalation owners assigned; I'm drafting a status blurb for the status page if you want me to push a preliminary note.

Sam (oncall): Quick runbook checks: disabling aggressive scale-in for pool-gpu-eu-a, force additional nodes, and kick the autoscaler into protective hold. Commands I'm running:
```
# temporarily increase desired capacity
gcloud compute instance-groups managed set-instance-template pool-gpu-eu-a --size=8
# pin autoscaler to hold mode
kubectl annotate namespace inference autoscaler=hold --overwrite
```

Jordan Reyes: Noted. I'll kick a canary capacity up in eu-west-1 from dedicated spare pool and reroute low-priority background jobs to delay. Creating a temp route via pool-gpu-eu-b.

Sam (oncall): Evictions stopped after bumping capacity, but we see a backlog of request tokens in the queue. Rolling restart of fronting pods to clear unhealthy connections.

DeployBot: Rollout: fronting-pods restart initiated by Sam at 1920004380 — success on 7/8 pods, 1 pod failed and got re-scheduled.

Alex Chen: Great. Once latency drops to normal for 10 minutes we'll de-escalate. Meanwhile let's capture action items for the post-incident follow-up. I'll nominate a postmortem lead.

Mira Patel: I'll own the postmortem and coordinate with infra and support. Proposed stakeholders: Alex (runtime), Jordan (capacity), Sam (oncall timeline), Priya (customer comms). Proposed timeline: 1) Postmortem draft in 48 hours, 2) Review session in 72 hours with SRE + Product + Support.

Priya (support lead): Support will push the status blurb now: "Investigating elevated latencies in EU-West-1 affecting inference API. Immediate mitigation in progress. We will update within 30 minutes." :rotating_light:

IncidentBot: Update: mitigation reduced 95th latency by ~55% at 1920004435. Monitoring for stabilization.

Sam (oncall): Latency back to baseline (~15% above normal) at 1920004450. No new 429s. I'm going to keep autoscaler in protective hold for 30m and then step down.

Jordan Reyes: For the remediation plan I propose:
- short-term (now): disable aggressive scale-in, allocate spare capacity, add temporary routing to eu-b
- mid-term (2 weeks): change autoscaler policy to avoid overlapping scale-in with maintenance windows; increase cooldown on scale-in from 300s to 900s
- long-term (quarter): add cross-pool proactive capacity buffer and improve preemption handling in the runtime

Alex Chen: Add one more mid-term item: implement a preemption-aware eviction handler in the node agent to drain gracefully when preemption is predicted. Also add a synthetic canary test that runs hourly to validate pool capacity under maintenance.

Mira Patel: Scheduling: postmortem doc draft assigned to me. Meeting proposed: 1920004321 + 72h => 1920026321 (approx). I'll create invite and link to doc in #eng-postmortems.

Priya (support lead): Action item for support: prepare a customer impact summary with affected tenants, time windows, and mitigation actions. Due: 24h. Owner: Priya.

Sam (oncall): Ops action items I captured:
- Sam: timeline + logs export to S3 + annotate where autoscaler actions happened. Due: 6h.
- Jordan: implement temporary routing and validate no cascade to other pools. Done.
- Alex: evaluate runtime fallback to lighter models to reduce token load during capacity pressure. Due: 3 days.

Mira Patel: Adding a tracking ticket in our remediation board: INF-8473 — "EU-GPU pool: autoscaler and preemption hardening". Linking to postmortem and customer comms.

Alex Chen: Let's also add a metric alert change: alert when node preemption rate > 4/hour for any pool AND queue length > 2000. Owner: Alex. Due: 48h.

Priya (support lead): I'll coordinate customer follow-up emails post-mortem. For now, updated status: customers notified; support escalators aware. :email:

Sam (oncall): Clear next on-call steps: keep protective hold for 30m, then monitor cooldown period. If backlog doesn't clear by then, escalate to infra lead for emergency scaling.

IncidentBot: Incident status: mitigated — monitoring — latest update at 1920004540. Severity: reduced to medium.

Mira Patel: Postmortem outline (I'll fill in):
- summary and timeline
- root cause analysis (maintenance + preemptions + aggressive scale-in)
- mitigations applied live
- action items (owners + due dates)
- validation plan

Jordan Reyes: I'll own the mid-term autoscaler policy update PR. Will include tests and a canary rollout configuration. PR target: in 7 days.

Alex Chen: Quick note: check cost impact of holding extra capacity for 30-60 minutes; finance will want an estimate. Jordan, can you add a rough figure to the remediation ticket?

Jordan Reyes: Yep. I'll put a delta-cost estimate in INF-8473 and flag for finance review.

Priya (support lead): I'm done with the status update for customers; pushing now. Will send postmortem summary once Mira's draft is ready.

Mira Patel: Posting the postmortem draft link here once created. Thanks everyone for the quick triage. Closing Slack thread when postmortem is scheduled and INF ticket is created.

Alex Chen: Thanks team. Follow-ups: Mira draft (48h), Support summary (24h), Autoscaler PR (7d), Runtime fallback eval (3d), Alert tuning (48h). I'll add these to the remediation ticket now.

IncidentBot: Incident closed for active paging at 1920004620. Monitoring continues for 2h.
